fixes.explanation: The text says the opposite. Mark 5:26 tells us she had been under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had, “…but to no avail.” Then it adds that “…her condition had only grown worse.” Twelve years of this, and she had spent all she had.
Mark 5:27 says she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak. That's what she does. She touches His cloak, and nothing more is said about how.
Nobody grabs a hand here. The text says she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak. It's a small detail, and it's the kind I'd have missed in a rush too.
The text doesn't have her calling out. Mark 5:27 says she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak. Her moment is a touch, not a shout.
He asks about a touch, not about needs. In Mark 5:30 He turns to the crowd and says, “Who touched My garments?” That's the question the text gives Him, and it points to one specific touch.

The disciples don't point at anybody. They answer, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’…” Their answer is about the crowd pressing in. Nothing in their words points to her.
They don't point her out. Mark 5:31 has them say, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’…” Their answer is about the crowd pressing in. It names no one.
Mark 5:33 says she came, fell down before Him trembling in fear, and “…told Him the whole truth.” She doesn't leave anything out. I think that took real nerve.
Right, no scolding. Mark 5:34 has Jesus say, “Daughter,” and then, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.” She came in fear, and He sent her off with those words.
Not so. Mark 5:40 says He put them all outside. Then He took the child's father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child. Those are the ones who go in with Him.
Right, not everyone stays. Mark 5:40 says Jesus put them all outside. Then He took the child's father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child.

Mark 5:41 gives us the words and the meaning right together: “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!” Jesus takes her by the hand and speaks directly to her. The writer even stops to translate it for us.
Mark 5:42 says, “Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around…” Jesus says get up, and she gets up. Right away, she's walking around.

Mark 5:43 says Jesus “…told them to give her something to eat.” After all that astonishment, there's a plain, practical instruction. I think it's a good reminder that even after a miracle, a hungry person still needs a meal.
